prompt:
Create a production 2D painted game sprite sheet, 1536x1024 with true transparent alpha background. Reference 1 is CHARACTER DESIGN ONLY: the King Down Ogre, enormous barrel chest, rounded belly, squat heavy bare feet, small bald head with heavy brow and two small lower tusks, oversized but anatomically coherent hands, plain knotted short skirt, thick terracotta wrist cuffs. Do not reproduce clay/3D shading or text. Reference 2 is STYLE reference: coherent hand-painted fantasy game illustration, clear angular brush shading, attractive restrained outlines, readable at small chess-board scale.
Exactly TWO complete full-body Ogre figures, arranged side by side in equal 768x1024 transparent cells. Left: warm IVORY skin and ivory skirt, subtle neutral shadows, terracotta cuffs. Right: dark CHARCOAL slate skin and charcoal skirt with readable light edge accents, same terracotta cuffs. Army colour overwhelmingly dominates; no green skin. Same character, same size and exact same pose in both cells.
Pose: standing in a stable wide stance, three-quarter side view facing RIGHT. Both arms held forward in a natural braced pushing-ready pose, elbows modestly bent, open hands at lower-chest height, palms facing RIGHT. Near hand foremost, far hand slightly behind/above but visibly separate. Hands have anatomically consistent fingers and thumbs; firm flat heel of palm contact surface. Keep arms proportionate to the large Ogre body, shoulders connected, wrists straight, no long dangling forearms. Character's expression determined, appealing, not grotesque.
Each figure entirely inside its cell with safe transparent margins: head around y170, feet soles around y890; entire body+hands from roughly x95 to x665 within each cell. Clear transparent gutter between the two. Full toes, heels, skirt and fingertips, no cutoffs, no pedestal, no floor/shadow, no weapons. Finished painted 2D art, NOT a 3D render, photograph or disconnected puppet parts. No lettering, guides, watermark or checkerboard. Preserve the Ogre identity while matching the Pawn illustration's painting language.
